stem: For the standard cell $\text{M}|\text{M}^{2+}||\text{Pb}^{2+}|\text{Pb}$, $E^\circ_{\text{cell}}=0.46$ V and $E^\circ_{\text{Pb}^{2+}/\text{Pb}}=-0.13$ V. Find $E^\circ_{\text{M}^{2+}/\text{M}}$.

verdicts.working: For the cell as written, E°cell = E°(Pb²⁺/Pb) − E°(M²⁺/M). Hence 0.46 = −0.13 − E°(M²⁺/M), so E°(M²⁺/M) = −0.59 V.

working:
$E^\circ_{\text{cell}}=E^\circ_{\text{cathode}}-E^\circ_{\text{anode}}$ 
$0.46=-0.13-E^\circ_{\text{M}^{2+}/\text{M}}$ 
$E^\circ_{\text{M}^{2+}/\text{M}}=-0.59\ \text{V}$

Independent check: For the cell as written, E°cell = E°(Pb²⁺/Pb) − E°(M²⁺/M). Hence 0.46 = −0.13 − E°(M²⁺/M), so E°(M²⁺/M) = −0.59 V.
solution:
For the cell as written, $E^ _{\text{cell}}=E^ _{\text{cathode}}-E^ _{\text{anode}}$.
$$0.46=-0.13-E^ _{\text{M}^{2+}/\text{M}} \quad\Rightarrow\quad E^ _{\text{M}^{2+}/\text{M}}=-0.59\ \text{V}$$
